Subject: Request: temporary standby activation lead time and data-loss acceptance

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We are finalizing our continuity plan for the payments service and need to raise one operational constraint from our side. Our security/compliance team requires a documented agreement for any deviation in activation lead time for multi-region failover during scheduled month-end processing windows (last 48 hours of the month).

Specifically, we want to request a temporary relaxation that tolerates a longer activation lead time (up to 45 minutes RTO) for warm-standby activation during that 48-hour window, and an RPO of up to 10 minutes for that same period, provided that Redwood commits to the standby handshake and post-failover reconciliation process you outlined. We are prepared to accept a bounded, documented tolerance if we have: 1) a clear activation runbook, 2) audit logs for the activation timeline, and 3) a defined compensation/credit schedule if activation exceeds the window.

Can you share what packaging of commitments Redwood can offer for this narrow operational carveout? We will need the wording for procurement and audit.

Best,
Neal

Thanks for the clear ask and for flagging the audit requirements. I looped in Sean (variance approvals) and Karthik (SDR/resilience design) so we can put a precise proposal together. A few clarifying Qs to make our amendment draft useful for procurement and compliance:

- Is the requested 45-minute RTO cap intended as a hard maximum for all failovers in the window, or only for customer-triggered/manual activations?
- Do you require point-in-time recovery guarantees for transactional systems, or is eventual reconciliation acceptable if you have compensating controls (e.g., pending queue with idempotency keys)?

Grace —

Quick technical note for the amendment draft. We can accommodate a temporary 45-minute activation SLA for a defined 48-hour window, but only with these constraints:

- Activation path: prefer automated cross-region routing with prefix cache warm-up. Manual operator activation may add unpredictable delays; if they require manual failover for audit reasons, we should mark the SLA as 'best-effort' rather than guaranteed.
- RPO: 10-minute target is feasible if persistent write-ahead logs are shipped to the standby region with <60s batching; that implies slight ingestion latency during the window and some extra egress cost.
- Observability: we'll produce an 'activation trace' (start/handshake/kv-sync/route-cut) and retain it for 90 days. Audit logs will include tokenized request ids and timestamps.
- Compensation: propose a tiered credit: 25% credit if activation >45m but <=90m; 50% if >90m; full SLA remediation conversation if data inconsistency events are detected post-failover.

I'll draft the exact legal-safe phrasing for the SLA amendment. Also want to flag INF-1248 (JIRA) to track the engineering tasks for the handshakes and testing.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Site Reliability, Redwood Inference

Neal —

Thanks for your patience. Attached is a first-pass package we believe will satisfy procurement and audit for the limited month-end window. Summary of the proposal below so your team can present it internally: 

1) Scope & window
- Applies only to the predefined month-end window (final 48 hours of each month) for 12 months (pilot period).

2) Activation commitments (temporary amendment)
- Target activation lead time (RTO) during the window: 45 minutes. If activation is initiated via our automated routing API, this is a guaranteed commitment. For manual activations initiated by BankPulse operators, SLA will be best-effort and excluded from credits.
- Target recovery point objective (RPO): 10 minutes for customer transactions during the window, subject to network egress constraints.

3) Observability & evidence
- Redwood will provide an activation trace for every failover event (start timestamp, handshake checkpoints, kv-sync completion, routing cutover). Traces retained for 90 days.

4) Compensation (credit schedule)
- Activation >45m and <=90m: 25% of monthly service fee prorated to the service impacted.
- Activation >90m: 50% credit and joint post-incident review.
- Material data-loss (unrecoverable loss vs. reconciliation delta) triggers escalation and remediation commitments beyond credits.

5) Controls & testing
- Quarterly joint failover tests (one canary during non month-end window, plus one dry-run inside the window annually) and a pre-month-end smoke test 72 hours before the window.

6) Next steps
- If this aligns, we'll circulate an amendment draft (attached SLA-amendment-draft.docx) and a DocuSign link for signature. We recommend BankPulse countersignature before the next month-end window to allow the engineering tasks (INF-1248) to complete.

Please find attached: BP-activation-runbook-draft.pdf, redwood-standby-handshake-diagram.png, SLA-amendment-draft.docx. DocuSign link included below in related links.

If you want us to tighten/loosen any of the items above (e.g., change retention, alter credits), we can iterate quickly.
